fieldValues.title: A reviewer reads an implementation ADR amendment as a ruling's surface: srs-web#703 escalated on Door 3 for amending ADR-021
fieldValues.summary: srs-web PR #703 (examples as ?open= links, unit semanticops.com#54) amends ADR-021 to add the editor request on a read-only link. The WG reviewer escalated: 'the PR amends ADR-021, which changes a ruling's surface (Door 3, outside the role's boundary)'. ADR-021 is srs-web's own architecture record, the amendment executes proposed decision D3 287c64f4, and the reviewer's own boundary (5739852c) says inside = execute an existing ruling. The question is whether an ADR in a code repository is a ruling (then every ADR amendment needs a programme decision first) or the group's record of how it executed one (then amending it is inside the boundary once the ruling exists).
evidence: srs-web PR #703 wg-quorum comment by agent:editor-reviewer, 2026-11-03: 'the PR amends ADR-021, which changes a ruling's surface (Door 3, outside the role's boundary)'
WG Agent-supported editor boundary 5739852c: inside = execute an existing ruling; outside = new rulings
srs-rust ADR-048 and srs-web docs/adr/ are implementation-side records; the programme's rulings are governance/decision records in the SemanticOps decision log
fieldValues.body:
- If ADRs are rulings, the group can never record its own execution without a session; if they are the group's records, the reviewer's Door 3 read is wrong and the handbook should say so.
- What to do instead, until ruled: a PR that amends a code-repo ADR cites the programme decision it executes in its Placement basis line; the reviewer checks the cited decision, not the ADR.
